passage: The physics coaching class had already started when Mahima and Rishabh slipped in together, ten minutes late, both holding umbrellas. Deepak, in the back row, sat up straight. Together? Again? He remembered them laughing at the canteen last week. He didn't know that Mahima's scooter had broken down and Rishabh lived on the same road. By the time the teacher wrote the first formula, Deepak's mind had written a whole story. He could already picture telling the boys at the tea stall. He'd be the one who knew first. Nobody would call him the quiet one then. His fingers itched towards his phone. "Deepak, the answer?" the teacher asked. He hadn't even heard the question.

qa.q: How late were Mahima and Rishabh to the coaching class?
qa.a: They were ten minutes late.

qa.q: Why was Deepak so eager to tell the boys at the tea stall?
qa.a: He wanted to be the one who knew first and to feel important, so no one would call him the quiet one.

qa.q: What could Deepak do at this spark stage to stop a rumour before it starts?
qa.a: He could notice that he is only guessing, since arriving together has many ordinary reasons, and keep the idea to himself or simply ask them later.

qa.q: What would change if Deepak knew about the broken scooter?
qa.a: His exciting story would fall apart, and he would see that two neighbours sharing a ride is ordinary news, not gossip.

grounding: It shows a teenager who sees two classmates arrive late together and, wanting to be first and look connected, treats his guess as news.

passage:
Hi Rekha didi,
How's snowy Canada? Here it's just exams and gossip. You will NOT believe what I saw today. Kavish and Tanu walked into assembly late, TOGETHER, and Tanu's hair was all messy, like she'd been running. I'm like 90% sure they're dating now. Nobody else noticed, I think I'm the first to know! 😅
I'm planning to tell my bench partners tomorrow. Honestly, being the one with news feels so good. Everyone always acts like I'm outside everything, and this time I'm not.
Okay, maybe it was windy outside. And maybe they just met at the gate. Mumma says I'm a nosy girl. But still!
Write back soon,
Simran

qa.q: What was Tanu's hair like when she came into assembly?
qa.a: Tanu's hair was all messy.

qa.q: What does Simran's line about always being outside everything suggest she wants?
qa.a: Simran wants to feel included and important, and being first with news gives her that feeling.

qa.q: What would you advise Simran before she tells her bench partners?
qa.a: To notice the doubts already in the email, the windy day and the gate, and treat it as a guess rather than news, keeping it private.

qa.q: How might Kavish and Tanu feel if Simran's guess spreads?
qa.a: They could feel embarrassed and misunderstood, especially if they just happened to walk in together.

grounding: It illustrates a teen who sees two classmates arrive late together and wants to be first with the news, so a guess starts to feel like fact.

passage:
The school gate in Aligarh closed at 8:15 sharp, and Yusuf was on late-duty with the prefects, writing names.

At 8:22, Tarun and Sana from 11B came running up the road together, both out of breath, both laughing.

Yusuf wrote their names. He also wrote, in his head, a whole story. Late together. Laughing. Same road. They must be going out.

By first period he was desperate to tell someone. It would be huge. He would be the one who knew first.

At break he leaned over to Irfan. "Guess who came in together this morning, late."

He didn't mention that Tarun lived in Sana's colony, or that the city bus had broken down on that road, which half the late kids had said. Those facts would have made it a much smaller story.

qa.q: At what time did Tarun and Sana arrive?
Why was Yusuf so eager to tell Irfan?
qa.a: He felt excited and wanted to be the first with big news, to seem connected and important.

qa.q: What could Yusuf have done before sharing his guess?
qa.a: He could have remembered the ordinary facts, the same colony and the broken-down bus, and kept his guess to himself.

qa.q: How might Tarun and Sana feel if the guess spreads?
qa.a: They would likely feel embarrassed and annoyed, having done nothing but miss the same bus.

grounding: Yusuf sees two classmates arrive late together and, wanting to be first with news, treats his guess about a relationship as a fact worth sharing.

passage:
Dear Tultul,

You won't believe what I saw today. Parveen and Imtiaz from our class came to the tuition centre together. Twenty minutes late. Parveen's hair was wet from the rain and Imtiaz was holding her umbrella.

I'm almost sure they're dating. I mean, why else would they come together, late, sharing an umbrella?

I haven't told anyone yet. I'm saving it for tomorrow at lunch. Everyone will want to know, and I'll be the first. Honestly, I love the feeling of knowing something before the others.

Okay, fine, I know Imtiaz lives in the same building as Parveen. And it was pouring. But still.

Write back soon and tell me I'm right.

Pallavi

qa.q: Why was Parveen's hair wet?
qa.a: From the rain.

qa.q: How does Pallavi feel about knowing this news first?
qa.a: Pallavi enjoys the excited feeling of being the first to know something before the others.

qa.q: What could Pallavi do before lunch tomorrow?
qa.a: Notice that her "almost sure" is only a guess, since they live in the same building and it was pouring, and not share it as a fact.

qa.q: How might Parveen feel if Pallavi's guess reaches the class?
qa.a: She would likely feel embarrassed and upset at being talked about for sharing an umbrella in the rain.

grounding: Pallavi's letter shows her treating a guess about two late classmates as a relationship, eager to be first with the news.

passage:
So you want to know how the whole mess started? I'm Kalyani, and honestly, it started with me.

It was the day of the science fair. I was setting up our volcano when Tarun and Mitali walked in together, forty minutes late, carrying the same box.

My brain just went: they're a couple. They came together. They're late. They're giggling. Obviously.

I didn't stop to think. I wanted to be the first to know. I wanted everyone to crowd around me and say, "What? No way!" So I texted two friends right there, under the table.

Later I found out Tarun's project partner had fallen ill and Mitali had helped him carry the box from his house. That's it. That was the whole thing.

But by then my guess had already become everyone's fact.

qa.q: Why were Tarun and Mitali carrying the same box?
qa.a: Tarun's project partner had fallen ill and Mitali helped him carry it from his house.

qa.q: What was Kalyani feeling when she texted her friends under the table?
qa.a: Kalyani felt excited and eager to be the first with news, wanting everyone to crowd around.

qa.q: What went wrong, and what could Kalyani have done instead?
qa.a: Kalyani shared a guess as if it were fact; waiting, or simply asking Tarun or Mitali why they were late, would have stopped it.

qa.q: What was it like for Mitali when the guess became everyone's fact?
qa.a: She probably felt embarrassed and unfairly talked about, just for helping a classmate.

grounding: Kalyani sees two classmates arrive late together and, wanting to be first with news, turns a guess about a relationship into a fact she shares.

passage:
Monday. Shankar saw Nisha and Farhan walk into first period ten minutes late, together, both a little breathless. Mrs Pillai marked them late without a word. Shankar's brain lit up. Together? Late? Something's going on.
Tuesday. He watched them all day. Farhan lent Nisha a pen. She laughed at something he said. Each tiny thing clicked into the picture Shankar had already drawn. He imagined telling the group and everyone turning to him: "How do you always know stuff, man?"
Thursday. At the bus stop Kishore asked, "Anything interesting this week?" Shankar opened his mouth, the story ready and polished. Then Kishore added, "Oh, did you hear Nisha and Farhan got stuck at the railway crossing on Monday? Same bus." Shankar shut his mouth. His big fact had only been a guess wearing a costume.

qa.q: Why were Nisha and Farhan late on Monday?
qa.a: They got stuck at the railway crossing on the same bus.

qa.q: What did Shankar want when he imagined telling the group?
qa.a: He wanted to feel important and connected, excited at the thought of everyone turning to him as the one who always knows.

qa.q: What could Shankar remember the next time a guess feels like news?
qa.a: He could separate what he actually saw, two people arriving late, from the story he added, and hold back until he knows the real reason.

qa.q: What would change for Nisha and Farhan if Shankar had told the group on Tuesday?
qa.a: They could have faced teasing and whispers about a relationship that did not exist, all because of a shared bus delay.

grounding: Shows a teen guessing at a relationship between two classmates who arrive late, with the wish to be first with news making the guess feel like fact.
